- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price is trending up.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 (neutral or negative), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch upward momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates mean reversion; if 10–15 days of price consolidation, forecast should be slightly above recent 10-day average.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/0.67), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.
